name: blur-veil
title: Blur veil
description: Shows an inert blurred teaser beneath a prompt; blur is presentation, not security. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

meta.whenToUse: A glimpse of the work should sit behind the invitation, so entering a code feels worth the effort.
meta.notFor: Protecting anything. The children stay in the DOM and travel to the browser; blur is a visual effect, not a boundary.
pitfalls: Never pass genuinely protected content as children while locked. Pass a representative sample, and render the real preview only once `unlocked` is true.
Locked children are inert and skipped by the keyboard. That is presentation, not authorization.
meta.contract: Shows an inert blurred teaser beneath a prompt; blur is presentation, not security. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

props.name: unlocked
props.description: Consumer-controlled access state; required. True removes the veil.

props.name: children
props.description: Preview content; required. Locked content remains in the DOM and is not secure.

props.name: prompt
props.description: Prompt rendered above the inert preview while locked; required.

props.name: blur
props.description: Blur radius in pixels, clamped to 0–30.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the prompt region.

props.name: theme
props.description: Explicit theme; omitted follows the system preference.

meta.a11y: Native controls, visible focus, localized labels; lifecycle messages use polite announcements. No modal dialog is created.

docs: UI only. Read https://knock.codes/docs/blur-veil.md. Consumers own authorization.
